content:
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a track record of taking infrastructure and system-design improvements from proposal through production.

At Tallybrook, I’m the technical lead of a five-person platform team operating eight EKS clusters across three regions and supporting approximately 350 services. I designed and built an internal developer platform adopted by all 14 product teams, reducing the time to take a new service to production from around two weeks to under a day. I’ve also led reliability and cost initiatives, agreeing an error-budget policy with product leadership and reducing on-call pages by approximately 60%, as well as reducing EC2 spend by 38% through a Karpenter and Spot migration.

This experience is relevant to shaping Corvale’s train-to-cloud infrastructure and taking it into production: designing and operating AWS environments, maintaining Terraform-based infrastructure, and working with product and engineering stakeholders to make systems reliable and straightforward to run. At Brightwater Games, I used k6 load tests to simulate 300,000 concurrent players and identified a connection-pool limit before launch. I would bring the same analytical, preparation-led approach to the connectivity platform, while contributing my AWS networking and platform experience to its system design and security considerations.

Corvale’s focus on teams owning their systems and solving problems collaboratively particularly appeals to me. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform and infrastructure experience could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.

Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It opens with a clear experience summary, uses credible metrics, and connects the candidate's platform work to Corvale's infrastructure and reliability needs. The examples are specific and persuasive: eight EKS clusters, 350 services, 14 product teams, a 60% reduction in on-call pages, 38% lower EC2 spend, and 300,000-player load testing. The main content weakness is that the letter remains more focused on Kubernetes platform engineering than on the role's specific train-to-cloud concerns, secure connectivity, networking, and infrastructure-as-code maintenance.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly parseable: it uses standard text, a conventional letter structure, and no problematic tables, graphics, headers, or unusual formatting. Relevant keywords such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, infrastructure, system design, observability, reliability, and stakeholder collaboration are present. AI screening probability is good because the letter contains quantified outcomes and direct role alignment, but it could be improved by using the job's exact terms more explicitly, particularly cloud environment design and operation, systems architecture, AWS networking, and technical proposals from idea to production. Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, and certificate management should not be added because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, analytical thinking, technical leadership, and stakeholder collaboration. It also aligns well with Corvale's engineering-led culture through its emphasis on ownership, reliability, self-service platforms, and making systems straightforward to run. The candidate does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM experience in the supplied material; these are genuine alignment gaps rather than document defects. Linux and virtual-machine experience exists in the candidate material but is not surfaced in the letter. The letter would be more compelling if it connected the Brightwater load-testing example and Tallybrook platform work more directly to telemetry ingestion, alerting, remote services, and train-to-cloud system design without claiming direct transport or IoT experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the third paragraph, replace the sentence beginning "This experience is relevant to shaping Corvale’s train-to-cloud infrastructure" with a more explicit, evidence-based alignment sentence: "This experience is relevant to shaping Corvale’s train-to-cloud infrastructure: I have designed and operated AWS cloud environments, maintained Terraform-based infrastructure, applied AWS networking knowledge across services including VPC and IAM, and taken platform and system-design improvements from proposal through production." This uses supported terms from the candidate material and the job description without claiming mTLS or certificate-management experience.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the paragraph beginning "At Tallybrook," make the leadership and stakeholder evidence more explicit by revising the reliability sentence to: "I led the introduction of SLOs and burn-rate alerts for 20 critical services, agreed the error-budget policy with product leadership, and reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%." This more directly demonstrates leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along, using facts already present in the candidate information.

MINOR, OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENT 3 — If space permits, add one short sentence before the closing: "Earlier, as a Linux Systems Engineer, I managed approximately 600 Linux servers, complementing my experience operating AWS-based platforms and virtual-machine infrastructure." This surfaces the supported Linux and EC2/VM background for a listed nice-to-have without overstating the experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well tailored to the Fleet Connectivity role. It leads with relevant experience, uses quantified outcomes, and connects the candidate’s AWS, Terraform, platform, observability, cost-optimization, and capacity-planning work to Corvale’s infrastructure challenges. The progression from current platform leadership to Brightwater’s analytical load-testing work and earlier Linux operations is logical. The closing is appropriate and avoids unsupported claims about location or working arrangements. The main content weakness is that it does not explicitly demonstrate every major requirement, particularly security, mTLS/SSL/TLS, and Terragrunt; however, these are gaps in the candidate’s evidenced background rather than defects that can be solved through rewriting.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard paragraphs, contains no tables or graphics, and includes strong searchable terms such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, AWS networking, VPC, IAM, Linux, system design, SLOs, and k6. Its likely AI-screening performance is strong for AWS platform/infrastructure and reliability work, but weaker for exact-match screening because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and practical security are not supported by the candidate information and therefore should not be added. The role title appears near the beginning, which is helpful. The document could be marginally stronger by using the job’s phrase “cloud environment design and operation” more directly, although the current wording already communicates this meaning.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment operation, Terraform, platform/system-design work, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, analytical thinking, and clear communication. It provides particularly credible evidence through the eight-cluster EKS platform, 350 services, 14 product teams, 60% reduction in on-call pages, 38% EC2 cost reduction, and k6 testing at 300,000 concurrent players. The candidate’s technical leadership and ability to bring stakeholders along are well supported by leading a five-person team, agreeing an error-budget policy with product leadership, and taking platform improvements from implementation to adoption. Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, certificate management, and specific practical security experience are not evidenced in the candidate material. IoT, automotive, train-to-cloud, remote-device integration, and JVM/full-stack experience are also not evidenced. Linux experience is supported, but virtual-machine experience is not explicitly supported by the original information. These are candidate-background gaps, not document-writing defects.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and supported by strong quantified evidence: team leadership, EKS scale, adoption across 14 product teams, a two-week-to-under-one-day improvement, 60% fewer on-call pages, 38% lower EC2 spend, and k6-based capacity testing. It demonstrates technical leadership, analytical thinking, stakeholder engagement, and production ownership. The main content weaknesses are that it does not directly address several important requirements, the system-design and cloud-design wording is stronger than the original candidate information supports, and the phrase about managing 600 Linux servers is unnecessarily repeated. The Corvale-specific connection is relevant but somewhat generic.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard headings-free letter structure, plain text, common job-related terminology, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It includes useful keywords such as AWS, EKS, Terraform, infrastructure, Kubernetes, platform, SLOs, error budgets, Linux, and k6. ATS matching would be stronger for the supported parts of the advert if the letter explicitly included the exact terms "Terraform modules," "Atlantis," "AWS networking," and "VPC." It should not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, or security terminology because those are not supported by the original candidate information. Overall, AI screening probability is moderate to high for infrastructure, AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, technical leadership, reliability, and analytical-thinking criteria, but lower for the complete requirement set because networking/security and Terragrunt evidence are absent.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform-based infrastructure, systems/platform improvement, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, analytical thinking, clear communication, Linux, and virtual-machine-related AWS experience. The candidate's strongest evidence is operating EKS at significant scale, building self-service platform capabilities, leading reliability improvements, managing Terraform and Atlantis workflows, and conducting large-scale load testing. The document does not establish Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, practical security awareness, IoT, automotive, remote-device integration, or JVM-based backend/full-stack experience. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects and should not be implied or invented. The letter also does not provide direct evidence for train-to-cloud connectivity, so its relevance to the fleet-connectivity domain is transferable rather than demonstrated.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the paragraph beginning "This experience is relevant to shaping Corvale’s train-to-cloud infrastructure," remove or soften the unsupported claim "I have designed AWS cloud environments" and the phrase "system-design improvements from proposal through production." Replace them with wording grounded in the original information, such as: "I have operated AWS-based platforms, maintained Terraform-managed infrastructure, and taken platform improvements from implementation through production." This prevents the letter from overstating the documented experience.

MINOR: In the same paragraph, replace the repeated phrase "approximately 600 Linux servers" with a single, more targeted reference. For example: "Earlier, as a Linux Systems Engineer, I managed approximately 600 Linux servers, complementing my experience operating AWS-based platforms." Remove the second occurrence at the end of the sentence.

MINOR: In the paragraph describing Brightwater Games, strengthen the supported Terraform match by changing "maintained Terraform-based infrastructure" to "managed approximately 40 Terraform modules with Atlantis for pull-request plan and apply workflows." This uses the advert's infrastructure-as-code context while adding precise evidence from the original candidate information.

MINOR: In the paragraph connecting the experience to Corvale, add the supported networking keyword without implying unsupported mTLS or TLS experience. For example, change "designed and operated AWS cloud environments"—after softening it as above—to "operated AWS environments and AWS networking, including VPC-based infrastructure."

Fix: replace the wording with the narrower, supported formulation specified in the improvement instructions.
